Re: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Reference Number: POC-570CD9F39B-59936
Member: Jordan Novak (Member ID W423994730)
Requested Service: Lumbar fusion, CPT 22612
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-18
Appeal Deadline: 2027-02-14

Dear Aetna Appeals Review Team,

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 22612 (lumbar spinal fusion), communicated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated August 18, 2026, reference number POC-570CD9F39B-59936. The stated reason for denial was that "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." I am submitting this appeal, together with additional records from my surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, MD, to complete the file and to demonstrate that this surgery is medically necessary.

1. Responding to the "incomplete documentation" finding

Aetna's own Spinal Surgery Precertification Information Request Form (Form GR-68893-2) states that documentation should include, among other things:

"Most recent operating physician note including: Documentation of all clinical findings, Detailed neurological/orthopedic examination, Current plan of care, Conservative therapy, including type, duration, and outcome; Physical therapy notes including initial and final PT visit with discharge note from licensed physical therapist; All formal radiological and imaging reports read by a radiologist (myelogram, CT, MRI, spinal X-rays); For spinal and SI joint fusions: documentation of nicotine status with quit date and negative nicotine lab result within 6 weeks prior to surgery, if applicable."

The enclosed records address each of these items:

- Clinical findings and exam: Dr. Lindqvist's note documenting neurogenic claudication and diminished sensation in both L5 dermatomes, with no bowel or bladder dysfunction, and a current surgical plan of care.
- Conservative therapy, type/duration/outcome: 8 weeks of supervised physical therapy (core stabilization and lumbar flexibility), 20 visits completed 2026-05-24 through 2026-07-19, with the physical therapy discharge note enclosed; 6 months of NSAID therapy with inadequate relief; a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-29 that provided only 2 weeks of partial relief.
- Physical therapy notes: initial and final/discharge PT visit notes are enclosed, as required.
- Imaging read by a radiologist: MRI lumbar spine and flexion-extension radiographs dated 2026-07-06, with radiologist report, showing grade I degenerative spondylolisthesis at L4-L5 with 5 mm of translation on flexion-extension views and severe central stenosis compressing the cauda equina.
- Nicotine status: I am a non-smoker/never a nicotine user, which I understand means the lab-test requirement referenced in the form ("if applicable") does not apply to me; I am attesting to this status in writing and my surgeon's note confirms it.

If any specific item from this list is still missing from the file Aetna reviewed, I am requesting in writing that Aetna identify exactly which document or data element is still needed, consistent with the plan's obligation to provide the specific reason for the determination, so that it can be supplied without further delay.

2. Medical necessity of the requested fusion

Aetna's Clinical Policy Bulletin Number 0743, "Spinal Surgery: Laminectomy and Fusion" (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/700_799/0743.html), is the medical policy that Aetna's own precertification form directs providers to consult for lumbar fusion requests. That policy states, as medically necessary:

"Lumbar laminectomy for individuals with a herniated disc when all of the following criteria are met... All other reasonable sources of pain and/or neurological deficit have been ruled out... and Member has signs or symptoms of neural compression (radiculopathy, neurogenic extremity claudication, myelopathy) associated with the levels being treated; and Advanced imaging studies (CT or MRI) indicate central/lateral recess or foraminal stenosis (graded as moderate, moderate to severe or severe; not mild or mild to moderate), or nerve root or spinal cord compression, at the level corresponding with the clinical findings; and Member has failed at least 6 weeks of conservative therapy... and Member's activities of daily living are limited by symptoms of neural compression."

My clinical record satisfies each of these elements at the L4-L5 level: 14 months of progressive low back and leg pain unrelieved by rest; neurogenic claudication limiting standing/walking to under 10 minutes; MRI-confirmed severe central stenosis compressing the cauda equina; and more than 6 weeks of supervised, well-documented conservative therapy (8 weeks of PT, 6 months of NSAIDs, and a corticosteroid injection) without lasting relief.

CPB 0743 also indicates, in a section addressing pelvic fixation, that separate criteria specific to lumbar fusion appear elsewhere in the same policy (referenced there as "criteria for lumbar fusion (in I.1.9)"), and that policy separately references "spondylolisthesis/instability" as its own basis for fusion (as distinguished from fusion for uncomplicated degenerative disc disease, which the policy elsewhere identifies as not medically necessary). I was not able to obtain the complete verbatim text of that lumbar-fusion-specific numbered list, and I am not quoting or reconstructing that section. I am asking Aetna to apply that section to the following facts, which I believe meet an instability-based indication for fusion rather than the "degenerative disc disease" indication the policy excludes:

- Imaging-confirmed grade I degenerative spondylolisthesis at L4-L5 with 5 mm of translation on flexion-extension radiographs, which is a radiographically documented measure of segmental instability at the level requiring surgery; and
- Severe central stenosis at the same level compressing the cauda equina, with corresponding neurogenic claudication and bilateral L5 sensory findings on examination; and
- Failure of more than 6 weeks of supervised conservative therapy, as detailed above; and
- No active infection, no untreated substance use, and non-smoker status, none of which are barriers under the policy.

Because decompression of this severe, symptomatic central stenosis at a spondylolisthesis level is being performed together with fusion, I ask that the reviewer apply Aetna's own instability/spondylolisthesis-based fusion criteria in CPB 0743 to this fact pattern, and, if the determination again turns on specific numeric or documentation thresholds in that section, that Aetna state those thresholds in writing so that my surgeon and I can respond to them directly.

3. Requested action

I am requesting that Aetna:
1. Reverse the denial and approve CPT 22612 (with any associated decompression/instrumentation codes requested by Dr. Lindqvist) as medically necessary; or
2. If any documentation is still considered incomplete, identify the specific missing item(s) in writing; and
3. Provide the complete text of the lumbar-fusion-specific medical necessity criteria in CPB 0743 (the section referenced elsewhere in that same policy as "I.1.9") that were applied to this request, so that the file can be matched against the plan's own stated criteria.

Enclosed with this appeal:
- Surgeon's (Dr. Lindqvist, MD) clinical note and surgical plan
- Physical therapy initial evaluation and discharge note (2026-05-24 to 2026-07-19, 20 visits)
- Medication/injection records (NSAID trial; corticosteroid injection 2026-05-29)
- MRI lumbar spine and flexion-extension radiograph reports, dated 2026-07-06, with radiologist interpretation
- [Nicotine status attestation / any additional records the surgeon's office provides]

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and provide your decision within the timeframe required under my plan and applicable law. This appeal is submitted within the 180-day deadline stated in the denial notice (by 2027-02-14).

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Jordan Novak
